title: Stabilize interleaved prefetch for usage heatmaps and reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Console usage heatmap queries with interleaved pagination and tenant-aware prefetch are seeing high tail latency and unstable p95/p99 due to cross-tenant cache thrashing and non-deterministic shard access patterns. We reproduce long tails on large customers and during query spikes (e.g., scheduled reports).

Symptoms observed: high variance in query latency across pagination offsets, KV cache hit rate drops to <10% under concurrent scans, CPU wait increases on console-query-workers, and increased DB read amplification.

Root cause hypothesis: current prefix-agnostic prefetch strategy requests pages ahead without shard alignment, which causes hot-shard thrashing when many tenants with different cursor offsets interleave requests. The KV cache and read coalescing layers evict useful entries prematurely and batching breaks up, increasing per-token work.

Proposed solution: implement a shard-aligned deterministic prefetch + tenant-scoped soft LRU to limit prefetch churn. Complement with adaptive overscan window that widens for sequential access patterns and narrows for random jumps. Add a lightweight hedging policy for tail requests and a per-query cache-hit instrumentation surface to drive automatic tuning. Also include a compatibility shim to fall back to current behavior when telemetry is missing.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (prototype): library changes in console-query-service to compute shard-aligned prefetch offsets and tenant LRU namespace (no behavioral change by default). Add telemetry (per-query KV hits, eviction rate). (ENG-77399-branch)
- Phase 2 (canary): enable deterministic prefetch for 10% of traffic, collect metrics and run benchmarks against synthetic workloads that model large-tenant interleaving.
- Phase 3 (rollout): progressive rollout to 50% then 100% with automatic rollback on error threshold.

Instrumentation and measuring: add new dashboard panels (console/queries/prefetch/kvcache-hit-rate, console/queries/prefetch/overscan-size, console/queries/latency-by-tenant). Acceptance criteria require p95 improved by >=30% on testbed large-tenant workloads and no regression (>3%) on p50 for small tenants.

Rollout risks and mitigations:
- Risk: decreased throughput during initial rollout if prefetch policy maladapts. Mitigation: start at 10%, fail closed to old behavior, and set aggressive fallback.
- Risk: correctness edge case for cursor semantics across pinned rollups. Mitigation: add deterministic validation tests and a small canary that runs validation queries comparing outputs.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood/example/console-prefetch-design (internal), perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/console-prefetch-canary, experimental PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1428
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage completed. Reproduced high p99 with synthetic interleaved scanner against prod-like dataset. Logged baseline: p95=1.8s, p99=3.9s for top-10 tenants. Captured heap profiles and cache traces.

2026-02-17 - Diego Marquez: Built microbench harness to simulate mixed pagination patterns (sequential, zigzag, random). Early prototype deterministic shard-aligned prefetch reduced simulated p95 by ~38% and improved KV cache hit rate from 12% -> 46% in bench runs. Branch: ENG-77399/shard-prefetch-proto. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1428

2026-02-18 - Priya Rao (PM): Reviewed approach. Concern about regressions for small tenants and scheduled reports that jump offsets. Requested adaptive overscan and fallback to legacy policy when telemetry indicates low sequentiality. Added labels and requested canary plan.

2026-02-19 - Diego Marquez: Added tenant soft-LRU namespace and telemetry counters. Wrote validation tests comparing outputs with current behavior across 2000 sample queries. Synthetic canary (10%) configured; collecting metrics. Deployed canary to staging and started 24h soak.
Measurements so far (staging soak 4h): p95 delta -34% on large-tenant traffic; KV hit rate median up to 41%. CPU per-request moved +6% in worst-case but tail reduced.

2026-02-20 - Engineering lead (Lin Zhou): Approve canary. Next: coordinate with infra for rollout window to prod Canary and pair with infra autoscaling to absorb CPU variance. Add rollback alert thresholds to the runbook.
